sa99278a19cdc43: China Merchants Bank is one of China’s leading commercial banks, investing continuously in claud-native technology, artificial intelligence, and digital infrastructure. As AI expands to more financial scenes, the platform needs to support large model training, fine-tuning, online access and other AI loads on nearly 10,000 heterogeneous accelerators.
s81e7cc0ac7f1a0: On this scale, simply increasing the accelerometers will not solve the platform’s efficiency problems. Training requires stabilizing capacity and high levels of ingestion.
sdcd0310b39a4e1: China Merchants Bank creates a unified control plane on Kubernetes while retaining two decorating paths. Both loads run in the Kubernetes Deproyment Pod, using Ray as a distributed running time: Twinkle is responsible for multi-tenant training, vLLM or SSLang provides online access.
s3620b6f5eebe80: In the load control layer, Kuue manages training queues, quotas and access; Prometheus and KEDA scale up inference services based on real-time demand signals; Hami Scheduling and allocate shared accelerator resources; Fluid expedites access to data sets, model weights and check points.

s18faef4c323dbf: Training requires stable and predictable resources
s2cfe6351c9602a: Distributive training is usually long-lived and based on insinuation, and only all work can start effectively if the Worker and accelerator cards are ready. In the absence of a sensory quota access mechanism, some Pod may be activated early enough to spare capacity while waiting for the remaining resources. At the same time, data sets and model weights need to be transferred between centralized storage and computation nodes; when data are not ready, assigned accelerators will have to wait.
s2bbfbeaf649c95: Inference has to follow the flow.
sd6d1e29a8fa7f8: Online reference is the opposite. Requests fluctuate with business flows, and response delays are more important than batch-processing in case of stow-off. Accelerators are set at peak loads, leaving a large amount of idle resources in the valley. Indentations can reduce waste, but when traffic returns, new copies must reload model weights to service requests. If start-up is slow or unpredictable, the platform team must keep additional copies and push up unit Token costs.
se79b3d2efd3b30: The fine-tuning requires solation without repeating the loading base model.
s265698983f7e14: LoRA finely updates only a few parameters, but the traditional “one tenant deployment” will still load the complete base model as it runs. 5 of the same models will create five base models, although smaller Adapter is different. Tenant status is soolation, GPS memory is duplicated and initialization occurs when running.
s7cc9cb5fb8f087: Therefore, sharing the compute pools requires different load strategies and separate processing of physical accelerator sharing and model reuse.

s4dc7fd27abc500: China Merchants Bank uses a self-study platform strategy based on Kubernetes, which combines several CNCF projects into unified training and inference capabilities. Training and reference allow for the selection of engines and strategies that are best suited to one another, sharing control floors, resource layers, data paths and monitoring systems.

s2f8531733f3ccc: Training frameworks, reference engines and models are different in speeds and should not be closely aligned.

s17bf556ce0ed7a: Kuue, KEDA, Prometheus, Hami and Fluid are connected through the Kubernetes primary interface without requiring a product to manage the entire model life cycle.
s141e78bed7cfa6: The shared base is composed mainly of CNCF hosting projects. Kubernetes, KEDA and Prometheus are graduation projects; Kueue is maintained by Kubernetes SIG Scheduling; Hami and Fluid are incubators.

s7e8bcc1fa6fa23: Common resources sharing and model sharing to solve different problems
s5ef576fc9a21d6: Hami decides how the physical accelerator capacity is distributed, and Twinkle decides how multiple LoRA tenants can re-use a base model. The former reduces the waste of compute resources, while the latter eliminates redundancy; the two cannot be replaced.
